name: Arc de Triomphe
overview: The Arc de Triomphe is one of Paris's most iconic monuments, standing majestically at the center of Place Charles de Gaulle at the western end of the Champs-Élysées. This triumphal arch honors those who fought and died for France during the Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars.
history: Napoleon commissioned this triumphal arch in 1806 after his greatest victory at Austerlitz, declaring to his soldiers: 'You shall return home through arches of triumph!' Ironically, Napoleon never saw it completed - he was exiled to St. Helena while it was still under construction, and his funeral procession passed under it in 1840. The arch honors not just Napoleon's Grande Armée but all who fought for France. In 1920, an unknown French soldier from WWI was buried beneath the arch, with an eternal flame lit in 1923 that has never been extinguished - even during Nazi occupation! The arch has witnessed France's greatest triumphs and darkest hours: Napoleon III's victories, the humiliation of Prussian troops marching through in 1871, Hitler's victory parade in 1940, and the joyous Liberation march by Charles de Gaulle in 1944. Every July 14th (Bastille Day), the President of France rekindles the flame and lays wreaths, making this not just a monument to past glory, but a living symbol of French national spirit.
highlights: Panoramic viewing platform with Champs-Élysées views
Relief sculptures including 'La Marseillaise' by François Rude
Tomb of the Unknown Soldier with eternal flame
284 steps to the top for 360-degree Paris views
tips: Use underground passage to reach the arch safely - never cross the traffic circle on foot! Climb at sunset for golden hour views down Champs-Élysées. Museum Pass holders get free entry. Allow 1-2 hours for visit including climb.
